title: Add SDK parity conformance fixtures + runner (429/Retry-After, network errors, request_id propagation)
author: Sabrina James
description: Motivation: As part of the cross-language SDK parity initiative, we need a shared, repeatable way to assert retry/timeout/error/streaming behaviors don’t drift across Python/TS/Go. This PR adds a conformance test runner and a first set of fixtures to the Python SDK CI, focusing on the highest support drivers: 429 handling (including Retry-After), retryable 5xx, and network transport failures. Scope: (1) a runner that reads a fixture manifest and executes scenarios against a local stub server, (2) fixtures for 429 w/ Retry-After (seconds + HTTP-date), 503 w/ optional Retry-After, and simulated connection reset/timeout, (3) golden assertions for: request_id propagation, retry_count surfaced in error metadata, respect Retry-After semantics, and bounded exponential backoff w/ jitter (using deterministic jitter in tests), (4) CI wiring so these run on PRs and main. Notes: These tests are intended to be shared conceptually across SDKs; the fixture format matches what Go is implementing in pr-635 and TS is implementing in their conformance harness work. This PR does not change runtime defaults; it only enforces them via tests. Checklist: - [x] Fixture schema doc + examples - [x] Deterministic backoff/jitter for repeatable tests - [x] CI job added and runs on ubuntu-latest - [x] Verifies Retry-After parsing: seconds and RFC 7231 HTTP-date - [x] Verifies request_id present on both retryable + terminal failures (INT-1182) - [x] Adds developer docs for running locally (make test-conformance) Related: ENG-5127 (conformance harness), ENG-5126 (error taxonomy), SUP-29477 (Retry-After ignored in some SDKs).

notable_snippets: Runner uses a deterministic jitter provider in tests: jitter_seed=1337 to ensure backoff bounds are assertable without flakiness.
test_plan: 1) Local: python -m pytest -q tests/conformance/test_conformance.py 2) Local via Make: make test-conformance 3) CI: Verify new job 'conformance (python)' runs in PR and on main, and uploads junit xml on failure 4) Manual sanity: temporarily set REDWOOD_MAX_RETRIES=0 to confirm fixtures fail as expected and provide actionable diff output (attempt counts + Retry-After parsing).

release_notes: Developer-facing: Python SDK CI now runs a conformance suite enforcing standardized retry behavior, including 429 Retry-After handling and request_id propagation. No runtime behavior changes in this PR.
